Ticket handlers must retain project authorization, project locks, ticket versions and board revisions. The framework cannot infer those rules.

docs.title: Shared multiselect controls
docs.text:
For controls contributing to the same native array, choice() accepts distinct id values and clearField: false; listId is derived from the native control ID and can be overridden explicitly. Put one empty marker before all of those controls. Repeating the bare marker between array entries would discard earlier selections when PHP parses the form. Closed role rows retain their native checkboxes and submit with the rest of the form; JavaScript only draws the dropdown. The component enhances controls in nafinity:fragment-updated containers and closes their popovers on nafinity:fragment-removing.

Short choice lists focus their labelled listbox rather than an anonymous popup. Arrow keys move between options; Home/End reach the first/last option, and Enter or Space selects it. Searchable choices focus the combobox and keep text editing keys available. Escape closes the choice and returns focus to its trigger. The application layout offers Skip to content as the first keyboard link, targeting the focusable main region.

docs.title: Reusable notices
docs.text:
Invitations, user administration, settings, exports and invoice drafts use the shared src/views/components/notice.phtml component. Invitation forms separate introductory guidance, form fields and delivery notices with consistent spacing.

Render reusable notices through the native partial helper:

<?= \Naf\Board\partial('components/notice', [
    'severity' => 'warning',
    'title'    => \Naf\I18n\t('Check before saving'),
    'message'  => \Naf\I18n\t('This change ends existing sessions.'),
]) ?>

message and the optional title are translated plain text; the component escapes both. There is no raw HTML argument. severity accepts notice, info (the default), warning and error. Unknown values fall back to info. Each variant has a local Material Symbols icon, its own colour and an accessible severity label. Errors use role="alert"; other variants use role="note". Use errors for actual failures rather than general guidance.

For a dynamic message, messageAttributes can carry trusted view attributes such as ['data-account-status' => true, 'role' => 'status']. The hook is on the message paragraph, so replacing its textContent preserves the icon. An empty notice without a title is hidden. Keep attribute names in application code; message and attribute values remain escaped. Shared styling lives in app.css, icons in icons.css. The ordinary application layout loads both. A standalone page using this component must also load those stylesheets.

Notice partials use the same override lookup as other views. Existing field() and choice() components remain the entry points for form controls; this component does not change form submission or introduce a second rendering layer.

docs.title: Shared token contract
docs.text:
src/Resources/public/assets/theme-tokens.json is the canonical catalog for built-in palettes, editable tokens and numeric bounds. Themes::compile() builds saved and preview CSS from it. tools/build-themes.php generates tokens.css as the shipped fallback. After changing the catalog, run:

php tools/build-themes.php
npx prettier --write src/Resources/public/assets/tokens.css

Components use the same semantic colors (--bg, --surface, --text, --muted, --line, --accent and status colors) and the derived scales: --font-N, --space-N and --radius-N. The common --font-size, --density and --radius values determine those scales. Use --radius-full for pills. Structural dimensions, such as panel widths, icon geometry and image aspect ratios, remain component dimensions.

Extensions should consume these tokens in their own stylesheets. User-supplied ticket colors remain ticket data. Explicit branding font/color settings apply to the brand word only and continue to take precedence there.

Stylesheet addresses contain a SHA-256 content version and can be cached for one year. A saved edit creates a new URL. An old uncached version returns 404; an already cached file may remain available until its cache expires. Theme definitions and revision state are read on the next request.

docs.title: Shared mail layout
docs.text: See host defaults and template overrides for the mail/... view contract and data-email-layout marker. Message producers share the same branding, CSS inliner and plain-text alternative.

docs.title: Enforce an optional WIP policy
docs.text: Core WIP values are advisory. The separately installable Composer example in examples/nafinity-wip-policy demonstrates an admission rule through native project settings and Change listeners. Creating, moving, reopening, restoring or transferring open work into a full column returns 409 and rolls back native database effects. Ordinary edits, reordering and departures remain available. Project managers can disable enforcement. See the versioned setup and policy reference; the example is not an independently published Packagist package.

docs.title: Extension reference
docs.text: Every definition's parameters, the contracts, storage, the browser lifecycle for contributed widgets, and the negative cases — an unknown key, a reserved id, a value the type refuses — are documented with the code that implements them, in docs/Extensibility.md of naf/board.

docs.title: Nafinity accounts and invitations
docs.text: With naf/board 0.1.6 or newer, invite people into a board, manage authorized accounts and issue one-use password recovery links. Installation roles and board membership remain separate.

docs.title: Inviting people and assigning boards
docs.text:
Invite person in installation settings and Invite new person in a board's member settings share the same invitation service. Choose an initial board, email and board role. The default is Member; only a current owner can grant Owner or Manager. Project custom roles follow the same permission checks as direct membership changes. With email delivery enabled, the form can send the invitation; otherwise it returns a link to copy and share. No administrator chooses the recipient's password.

The recipient opens the link, enters a name and their own password, and immediately reaches the inviting board. The email is bound to the invitation and cannot be changed at registration. The password follows the same 15-character/72-byte rule as password changes. New invited accounts receive only the selected board membership, with no installation role or right to create projects. An invitation does not set email_verified_at: administrators may copy links, so possession alone does not prove delivery to the named mailbox.

Use Search accounts in another board's member settings to add that person later. After two characters, autocomplete finds active accounts by name or email, and selecting a result fills the email. A complete email also works without JavaScript. Only people allowed to manage members of that board can use the directory; it returns at most 20 names and email addresses. Adding existing accounts continues to use the regular membership service and its role checks. Already existing accounts cannot be recreated through an invitation. If an account is created after a link was issued, its owner must sign in with that account before joining. Existing active membership and credentials are preserved.

Links expire after seven days, can be used once and can be revoked under Pending invitations. Inviting the same address to the same board again replaces the previous link. Different boards can have separate invitations. Acceptance rechecks the inviting person's current membership, role permissions, the custom role and the board's archive state. Revocation, expiry, loss of the sponsor's rights, archiving and project deletion prevent registration through that link. Registration, membership assignment and consuming the token commit together. The database stores only the SHA-256 token hash; audit events contain no invitation token or email.

The public link and confirmation pages use Cache-Control: private, no-store and Referrer-Policy: no-referrer. Creation, searches and acceptance use NAF's persistent rate limiter; all writes require native CSRF protection. The public URL comes from app:url, not the request's Host header. Email is sent synchronously through NAF's Mailer. A delivery failure returns 503 and preserves any previous invitation. SMTP and SQL cannot commit atomically: a delivered link can be unusable if a later event or commit refuses the write.

M202610100001ProjectInvitations adds project_invitations. The public contract is InvitationServiceInterface; UI entry points call it rather than creating accounts directly. Installation administrators retain the programmatic AccountServiceInterface::create() API for provisioning. Regression coverage lives in InvitationTest, InvitationOverHttpTest and the browser account-search tests.

docs.title: Find accounts
docs.text: The installation's Users card uses a searchable table, ordered by name and id, with at most 50 accounts per page. Search matches literal name/email substrings; % and _ are not wildcards. A row opens an account editor in a separate native dialog. Editors are fetched on demand rather than rendered for every account. The primary invitation action sits at the top right above the table.

docs.title: Manage an account
docs.text:
The editor starts with account details: name, email and active status. It shows the account source, creation time in UTC and email verification state. Roles and access appear in a separate collapsed section. Each place has one compact row: the board label on the left and its directly assigned roles on the right. A pencil disclosure reveals the existing searchable multiselect; several roles can be held on the same board. Global, all-board and individual-board grants remain separate. Changing a selection updates its summary; Save roles submits all rows together, including closed rows, through the native RBAC endpoint and privilege policy. Grants in unavailable or archived scopes are displayed read-only and preserved. Your own roles and roles viewed without rbac.manage have no edit controls.

Disabling an account preserves its content, roles and memberships. You cannot disable your own account or the last active installation administrator.

Reading requires settings.manage and users.view. Editing also requires users.manage. The current permissions of the target must be contained in the actor's permissions in every scope the target can reach: editing credentials must not bypass private board or administrator boundaries. Administrators have the account capabilities. Password recovery additionally requires the separate users.reset_password permission, so delegating account edits does not implicitly delegate password recovery.

POST /settings/users/{user} accepts name, email, active (0 or 1) and the editor's opaque revision, plus CSRF. Unknown fields are refused. Writes lock current roles, permissions, grants and affected accounts before reauthorizing. An outdated revision or unavailable email returns 409 without changing data. The UI preserves failed edits and asks the person to reopen a stale editor. Changing name preserves sessions. Changing email or status increases the native security version, invalidates all prior sessions and pending account recovery and email-change links; a new email is unverified. Changing your own email asks you to sign in again. The old address receives the existing security notice.

Externally managed accounts show their source. Their display name and activation can be edited, but their email and password remain with their sign-in provider.

docs.title: Recover a local password
docs.text:
For an active local account, Create reset link creates a random one-use link, valid for 30 minutes. Optionally send it using configured mail; otherwise copy it and pass it privately to the person. The link uses app:url, never the request Host header. Only its SHA-256 hash is stored. A new link replaces the old one. Issuing a link leaves the password and sessions intact.

POST /settings/users/{user}/password-reset takes the account revision, optional send_email (0 or 1), and CSRF. Issuance is limited to 20 attempts per actor/hour and 3 per target/15 minutes. A mail failure refuses the operation and preserves the previous link. JSON responses expose the link only to the authorized actor; plain forms redirect to an authorized, one-time result page.

The recipient opens GET /password-reset/{token} and submits a new password with confirmation and CSRF to the same path. The native password rule requires at least 15 characters and at most 72 bytes. The page reveals no account identity, uses no-store and no-referrer, and never echoes password input. Consumption checks expiry, account activation, credential version, bound email and the issuer's current rights again under locks. Revocation of issuer rights makes outstanding links unusable. A concurrent second consumer receives 410.

Success atomically writes the password, consumes the link, invalidates pending email changes, increases the security version and queues a security notice. The recipient signs in normally afterwards; recovery never creates a session. Invalid and expired links return 410. Consumption is rate limited per token and peer. Maintenance removes expired rows. Database-backed audit events participate in the transaction; a failing listener refuses the write. External mail delivery cannot be rolled back and may contain a link that a later refusal invalidates.

Account audit data records the changed field names, without credential values, email values or raw recovery tokens.

docs.title: Update global roles
docs.text:
Select individual rows or all eligible rows on the current page to reveal the bulk action bar with its Update action. Search and pagination clear the selection. The confirmation form states the target count and requires explicitly enabling each property; unselected properties are omitted, and empty strings, false and null remain values when their field type accepts them. Own-account rows cannot be selected. The compact selection controls retain native keyboard and screen-reader behavior; disabled controls show a lock, and the page selector marks partial selection.

The initial properties add or remove one global role. These operations merge with current grants, preserve other roles and every scoped grant, and are idempotent. Scoped roles remain in the individual editor: board membership has additional rules and must not be inferred from a global grant operation. The role choices are restricted to the actor's current authority. Account names, credentials, account activation and personal preferences are not mass editable.

docs.title: Initial HTTP surface and guarantees
docs.text:
GET /settings/users returns the bounded table fragment (users_q, users_page). GET /settings/users/{user} returns a single editor. Both require current login, settings.manage and users.view, and successful fragments are not cacheable. POST /settings/users/bulk additionally requires users.manage, rbac.manage, CSRF and the privilege policy for every target. Its body contains only explicit targets and a values patch (initial keys: add_role, remove_role). Adding and removing the same role in one request is refused as ambiguous.

Global role definitions, their permissions and global assignments are locked before the privilege snapshot is read; selected accounts are checked under locks. This deliberately serializes global privilege batches. It avoids widening rights from a stale role definition. Changes dispatch the existing GrantsChanged events inside the batch transaction, so audit listener failures roll back the grants too. Listeners must keep external side effects out of this transaction.

Regression coverage checks bounded reads, lazy editors, literal searches, CSRF, unauthorized reads/writes, malformed selection, self protection, privilege reach, role preservation, idempotency, multiple-property merging, contributed field types and full rollback after a later property write fails.

docs.title: If the result is different
docs.text: Symptom Check The reset-link action is unavailable Check users.reset_password separately from account-edit rights; role synchronization preserves existing role definitions. An invitation or reset link is no longer valid Check expiry, revocation, current sponsor/issuer rights and the target account's current state. An account editor reports a conflict Reopen it to obtain the latest revision before applying the change. Email delivery fails Verify the configured transport; the operation preserves the previous invitation/reset link on a delivery failure.

docs.title: Nafinity appearance and configuration
docs.text: Administrators with settings.manage can configure public identity, interface themes, outgoing email design and installation values in naf/board 0.1.6 or newer. Personal theme and brightness choices remain independent.

docs.title: Use one public identity
docs.text:
Open Global settings → General → Appearance & landing page to choose the application name and upload a PNG, JPEG or WebP logo. The same identity appears in navigation, sign-in, public account pages, browser titles and favicon, the local AI assistant, notification preferences and outgoing email. The branding wordmark's chosen font and color also apply to the email header. A logo in email uses the public application URL; configure app:url to an HTTP or HTTPS address that recipients can reach.

New invoice drafts use the application name in their external reference. The reference is frozen with the provider payload when the draft is prepared. Renaming the application does not change a prepared or previously submitted reference. Older drafts display the reference from their stored provider payload so a person can still find an uncertain submission in the external invoicing account.

Technical names such as Composer packages, namespaces, commands, configuration paths, browser storage keys and AI tool identifiers retain their existing names. Demo board names and the documented demo password identify fixture data; changing the application branding does not rename projects or change credentials.

docs.title: Design outgoing email
docs.text:
An administrator with settings.manage opens Global settings → General → Email design. Choose the background, surface, text, secondary text, border and accent colors, then adjust font family, base size, corner radius and spacing. The design is global; a recipient's personal application theme does not change sent email.

The live preview uses sample data. Switch between invitation, password reset, email verification, security notice and notification, and choose Desktop or Mobile width. Previewing sends no email and does not save the draft. Save email design applies it to subsequent messages; Reset email design restores server defaults. An outdated configuration revision is rejected rather than overwriting a newer edit.

Click Send a test email to me to send the selected sample with the current unsaved design through the configured mail transport. The server resolves the signed-in account's current email address; the action cannot send to another recipient. It does not save the design, create a real invitation/reset code or change notification preferences. Automatic preview updates never send mail. Three test emails per account per minute are allowed. A transport failure keeps the draft intact and asks you to check email configuration.

The preview and sender use the same HTML renderer and CSS inliner. Colors and scale variables are resolved to literal values before CSS is embedded into the elements. Email clients support different CSS features; check important layouts in the intended clients as well as in the browser preview. No remote fonts are loaded.

docs.title: Grouped settings and modal navigation
docs.text:
General contains branding and landing page, interface themes, email design and advanced display options. Technical application values and activity-log retention appear under Application & activity log when advanced settings are enabled. Opening a child settings card keeps its parent underneath. The parent moves upward and leaves a named navigation header. Each ancestor header stays operable through the active dialog, while background forms remain inert. Clicking its title returns to that dialog by closing only its descendants, newest first. The separate close button also closes the chosen dialog; the oldest close button closes the whole stack. A dirty or busy dialog can stop the cascade through its normal cancel guard. Deep stacks keep all ancestor names available in a scrollable strip. Closing a child restores its parent's position, scroll and focused trigger. Unsaved form fields stay in their original DOM nodes. The native stack has no fixed logical depth; the visual offset is bounded to fit the screen. Reduced motion skips animations. Direct links such as #themes and #email-design restore the same parent hierarchy.

Project and installation role lists open their existing edit/create forms in child dialogs. Columns, swimlanes and labels use those same editors for existing entries and additions, while reorder controls stay in the parent list. Board members open Add member or Invite a new person over the unchanged list and pending invitations. The theme library and installation default stay in the parent; choosing or importing a theme opens its editor with the live preview. Closing an editor preserves its draft and returns focus to the trigger; saving uses the existing endpoints and restores the containing settings card. Without JavaScript these forms remain native disclosures.

The installation's people directory also uses the shared settings shell for account details, inviting a person and bulk changes. Search and selection remain in the parent list; children share its stacking, ancestor navigation, close controls and focus restoration. Invitation and bulk forms retain their existing authorization and submission paths.

Extensions can set parent: 'application' or another same-scope section id on Naf\Board\Definition\SettingSection. The generic renderer handles child cards and modal shells without feature-specific JavaScript. Authorized children of a removed or hidden parent appear at the root; cyclic parent definitions are rejected. New dialogs opened through the existing data-dialog controls or shared assets/dialog.js receive stacking, parent suspension, focus restoration and animated exit automatically.

Theme and email previews use sandboxed inline HTML documents with no scripts. Theme samples no longer load a separate page into the frame, so the installation can retain X-Frame-Options: DENY and frame-ancestors 'none'. Both previews keep their styles isolated from settings and use the modal body as their scroll container. Theme samples allow local stylesheets, icons and fonts from the exact HTTP origin, including the port, so Firefox also renders their inline documents. The installation does not need to relax its frame protection. Hosts that map an internal web-server port to a different public port can encounter a request-authority limitation in naf/framework 0.2.10: the preview may retain the internal port in its asset origin. Verify the preview at the public address; mapped-port deployments need the framework correction before relying on this preview path.

docs.title: Manage themes
docs.text:
An administrator with settings.manage opens Global settings → General → Themes. Choose a built-in palette as a template, enter a name, adjust typography, corner radius, spacing and the separate light and dark colors, then save. The isolated preview updates while typing and uses the same compiler as the saved stylesheet. Changes in the preview do not affect the installation.

Publish for all users makes a saved theme selectable in personal settings. Leave it off to keep a draft. Choose any published theme as the installation default; anonymous pages, including sign-in, use that default. Each person selects their theme in the account's personal settings, independently of the Light, Dark or System brightness setting. Installation default follows future administrator changes. Existing explicit Classic or Anthracite choices remain explicit after migration; new preferences follow the installation default.

Copy a theme to edit a separate variant. Built-in palettes remain available. Deleting or unpublishing a personally selected theme falls back to the installation default without rewriting that person's stored selection. A theme currently used as the installation default must be replaced before it can be deleted or unpublished. Theme names and definitions are installation data, not project-specific settings.

docs.title: Custom CSS, import and recovery
docs.text:
Custom CSS is loaded after the application's component styles and generated variables. Reuse semantic variables and the shared scales instead of repeating literal colors or spacing. For example:

.ticket-detail {
    border-top: 2px solid var(--accent);
    padding-top: var(--space-16);
}

The example assumes a Nafinity ticket view. It changes the existing .ticket-detail component without changing its stored content. Use html[data-theme='dark'] for dark-only rules, and @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) with html[data-theme='system'] for System mode.

CSS is limited to 32 KiB of UTF-8 and checked with a strict CSS parser. Imports, resource URLs, image resource functions and active legacy CSS syntax are rejected, including escaped forms. Themes support local CSS customization; they do not install remote fonts or fetch third-party stylesheets. Custom CSS can still hide controls or affect readability. The editor's sample runs in a sandboxed iframe without scripts or form submissions, so an unsaved rule cannot hide the surrounding editor.

Export downloads a versioned JSON document. Import theme validates it before replacing the editor draft; save to persist it. Theme files can be up to 64 KiB, including their JSON envelope. The installation supports up to 16 custom themes plus its built-ins. Theme configuration is stored through the existing encrypted installation configuration store, with the same revision conflict checks and audit trail as other global settings.

If saved CSS prevents normal use, open /settings?appearance=default#themes. That request uses the built-in standard stylesheet and skips custom theme CSS. The bypass does not change anyone's preferences. Theme saves return to this safe editor address. Restore server defaults removes the administration override for nafinity:themes; host configuration remains the default source.

Published theme CSS is public, including custom CSS and literal text inside it. Keep credentials and private data out of theme definitions.

docs.title: Add custom email CSS
docs.text:
Custom CSS is applied after the shared base styles and before inlining. Use the stable layout classes .email-header, .email-brand-name, .email-title, .email-content, .email-intro, .email-paragraph, .email-button, .email-highlight and .email-footer.

.email-title {
  color: var(--accent);
  padding-bottom: var(--space-16);
}

.email-button {
  border-radius: var(--radius-8);
}

The designer uses the same semantic names and scale catalog as interface themes: --bg, --surface, --text, --muted, --line, --accent, --on-accent, --font-family, --font-size, --radius, --density, --space-*, --font-* and --radius-*. Font stacks use the shared System, Serif and Monospace choices. Use simple var(--name) references to these known tokens. The validator rejects unknown variables, invalid values, imports, resource URLs and active CSS. Custom CSS is limited to 32 KiB. Email layout is table based and does not require scripts.

docs.title: Host defaults and template overrides
docs.text:
The typed installation setting appearance.email maps to nafinity:email_design. It holds common, colors and css; omitted common and color entries inherit the shared email defaults. Only installation administrators can read or write the preview and save endpoints. Generic settings API writes run the same validator.

Board message producers use Naf\Board\Mail\Messages and native mail/... views. The shared mail/layout contains the branding and stable CSS classes. Messages have HTML and a plain-text alternative with their action URLs. A host can override an individual view or the shared layout through its existing view paths. A custom layout without data-email-layout is left intact and is responsible for its own styles; layouts retaining that marker participate in the shared design inliner.

docs.title: If the result is different
docs.text: Symptom Check Changes appear only in the preview Save the email design; drafts do not change outgoing messages. A newer edit is reported Reload global settings and apply the edit to the latest revision. A custom rule is rejected Check CSS syntax, token names, the 32 KiB limit and resource URL restrictions. A test email does not arrive Check the configured mail transport and recipient account address; a successful send means the transport accepted the message, not a guarantee of inbox placement. A logo is missing in a recipient's client Check the public app:url and whether that client blocks remote images. A host template ignores the design Keep data-email-layout on the layout body to use the shared inliner, or maintain the override's own styles.

docs.title: Installation configuration
docs.text:
Global settings use the same typed fields and cards as personal/project settings. Every leaf of the merged server configuration is described automatically; provider metadata supplies choices, ranges and secret fields, including SMTP configuration. Lists and structured values use JSON. Existing application definitions and extension replacements take precedence over generated fields.

Installation settings initially show the standard fields and cards. The native Advanced settings switch reveals generated configuration cards below them and an Advanced settings fieldset below standard fields in mixed dialogs. The view preference is kept per administrator in the current browser tab; it does not change configuration. Hidden advanced controls are disabled and omitted from saves, so a standard-field save preserves all advanced overrides. Direct links to advanced cards reveal the advanced view. Extensions can opt fields in with advanced: true on SettingDefinition (the default remains false).

New scalar, nested and list entries in the host's config.php are discovered on the next request without a schema registration; lists use JSON and secret-like paths retain the shared write-only treatment. A central display glossary capitalizes known abbreviations such as MCP, RBAC, API, SMTP and IMAP; unknown words are humanized and explicit provider labels take precedence. Literal configuration paths remain unchanged.

The source next to each field distinguishes administration overrides, environment references, server configuration and declared defaults. Editing a field selects an administration override. Choosing Server configuration deletes that override; Clear value stores an explicit null where allowed. Passwords are write-only: a blank password input retains the previous value. Secrets never appear in HTML, JSON read responses or audit payloads.

Writes require installation settings.manage and native CSRF validation. The global endpoint is GET/POST /api/settings/application; values cannot be written into personal preferences. Form revisions reject stale edits with 409. Validation is all-or-nothing; database changes must connect to an existing application database where the current administrator remains active and authorized. Existing mail adapters validate active mail configuration without sending a message. The audit records changed/reset keys.

Overrides load before any plugin boots through the framework's config_sources.php convention, so database, sessions, auth and mail see the same values. They live outside the database in storage/configuration/values.enc, encrypted through the existing token cipher, with a generated key beside it. The directory is private (0700), files are 0600, and writes are locked and atomic. All application processes/replicas must share this private storage; back it up with its key. The key's protection rests on filesystem access.

New requests read the saved configuration; restart already-running queue/schedule/socket workers after changing their configuration. If a start-critical override prevents boot, set the process environment NAFINITY_CONFIG_OVERRIDES=0 and restart affected processes to recover using server configuration. Restore a valid encrypted file and its key, or move storage/configuration/values.enc aside, before removing the recovery override. The fixed storage location and recovery switch deliberately remain outside editable config.

Custom mail transports may implement ConfigurableTransportInterface::configurationFields() to return colon-separated config paths with label, type, default, index, options and sensitive metadata. This optional contract extends the existing transport interface; it introduces no dependency on Board or its renderer. Extensions can also declare application SettingDefinition values with configKey using the existing registry.

docs.title: Deploying Nafinity containers
docs.text: Deploy the public Nafinity image from GitHub Container Registry with persistent MariaDB and private application storage. This guide covers a first installation, updates, backups and restoration on a single Docker host.

docs.title: What you deploy
docs.text:
The official image contains the Nafinity installation and the published Composer packages recorded in app/composer.lock. It includes PHP, nginx, the queue worker, the scheduler and published assets. Composer and development source mounts are absent. compose.production.yaml adds MariaDB and separate persistent volumes for the database and storage/. Use one application instance with this template.

The repository's default branch is main. Each merge builds and checks native amd64 and arm64 images before publishing ghcr.io/nafphp/nafinity:main, latest and a full sha-<commit> tag. A stable GitHub release named vX.Y.Z also publishes X.Y.Z and updates latest. The latest tag follows the most recent successful main or stable-release publication; use a tested digest for a repeatable production deployment. Pull requests run the same checks without publishing. Multi-platform images include build provenance and an SBOM. High or critical Trivy findings block publication; the build upgrades Alpine packages before installing PHP.

Use main for staging. For production, select a tested version or digest from the Nafinity package page. A digest identifies the exact image; version and branch tags are registry pointers. A Board source merge alone does not update this image: release the Board package, update the installation's lock in a reviewed PR, then build the installation image.

The official package is public and needs no registry login for pulls. The workflow publishes with its own GITHUB_TOKEN. If you publish under your own namespace, GitHub creates a private package initially; an owner must set its visibility before an anonymous pull can work. See GitHub's container registry guide.

docs.title: Build your own installation
docs.text:
The official image includes this repository's host configuration. To add your own code, configuration or plugins, change the installation and build a new production image from its committed Composer lock:

make image IMAGE=ghcr.io/YOUR_NAMESPACE/nafinity IMAGE_TAG=YOUR_TAG
bin/check-production-image ghcr.io/YOUR_NAMESPACE/nafinity:YOUR_TAG
docker login ghcr.io
make publish IMAGE=ghcr.io/YOUR_NAMESPACE/nafinity IMAGE_TAG=YOUR_TAG

Replace YOUR_NAMESPACE with your registry namespace and YOUR_TAG with the version or build identifier you intend to publish. Authenticate with an account that can push there, using Docker's password prompt. Both commands use the same IMAGE and IMAGE_TAG values. Defaults are ghcr.io/nafphp/nafinity and sha-<current full Git commit>.

make image builds the production Dockerfile target from the committed Composer lock and tags the resulting local image with the chosen tag and latest. make publish pushes those two existing tags without rebuilding. It refuses missing tags or tags referring to different local images; rerun make image with the same settings before publishing. A local build contains the working tree at build time, so commit/review changes before using its default SHA tag.

Local builds target the Docker host's architecture. Official GitHub Actions publishes the combined amd64/arm64 image after both native checks pass. A manual push to the same moving tag replaces its manifest; use a separate namespace for your own host image. Configure the checked registry digest in NAFINITY_IMAGE. Runtime environment files and storage stay outside the image. See Nafinity extensions for application overrides and plugins.

docs.title: Prepare a first installation
docs.text:
Install Docker Engine with the Compose plugin on a Linux host. Keep a checkout of the Nafinity installation for the Compose file and deployment helpers. Image content comes from the registry; the checkout does not become a source mount.

From that checkout on the Docker host:

cp .env.production.example .env.production
chmod 600 .env.production

Set NAFINITY_IMAGE to the selected release tag or digest, NAFINITY_APP_URL to the public HTTPS origin, and two different random database passwords. Configure DNS and allow ports 80 and 443. The template publishes only nginx; MariaDB has no host port. SMTP credentials belong in the private environment file. Verify the actual SMTP provider before using invitations or password resets. Enable Mail-to-Ticket only after configuring and testing its mailbox and actor account.

Provide a valid certificate chain as deploy/tls/fullchain.pem and its private key as deploy/tls/privkey.pem. The container runs as uid/gid 1000. Give that identity read access to both files and directory traversal, while keeping the private key unavailable to other host users. Configure certificate renewal on the host; after replacing the files, run bin/production exec -T app nginx -s reload. The image does not issue or renew certificates. HTTPS and APP_ENV=prod are required. The production CSP allows same-origin connections; live WebSocket updates are disabled in this template.

bin/production always selects the production Compose file, environment and project explicitly, even when the development .env contains COMPOSE_FILE. It does not change or stop the development installation.

bin/production pull
bin/production up -d --wait db
bin/production run --rm --no-deps -T app php vendor/bin/naf db:migrate up
bin/production run --rm --no-deps -T app php vendor/bin/naf rbac:sync

Create the first account with a password read from the terminal. Run this block in Bash; the password stays out of command arguments and shell history:

read -r -s -p 'Administrator password: ' admin_password
printf '\n'
printf '%s' "$admin_password" | bin/production run --rm --no-deps -T app \
    php vendor/bin/naf nafinity:user admin@example.com 'Administrator' --admin
unset admin_password
bin/production up -d --wait app
bin/production exec -T app php vendor/bin/naf nafinity:assets:check

Sign in at the public URL and create the first project. Production refuses demo seeding. The health check verifies the web endpoint, database/schema, attachment storage and worker/scheduler heartbeats. It tests TLS locally without validating the public certificate name; separately check the public URL with certificate verification enabled. Monitor that external check and unhealthy containers.

docs.title: Back up and verify restoration
docs.text:
The production helpers work with named storage volumes. The development backup commands target the development bind mount and must not be used for this stack.

mkdir -m 700 -p /srv/nafinity-backups
bin/production-backup /srv/nafinity-backups/2026-10-13
bin/production-verify-restore /srv/nafinity-backups/2026-10-13

Choose a new directory for every backup. The backup stops the application and its bundled writers, saves a consistent database/storage snapshot, hashes every storage file and restarts only application containers that were running. Treat any nonzero exit or missing SHA256SUMS as an incomplete backup. Files include private attachments, OAuth state and sessions: encrypt and copy backups off the host, restrict access and set a retention policy.

The verification command creates disposable database and storage volumes under a separate Compose project. It imports the dump, compares all restored storage hashes, checks readiness and assets, reports restored row counts and removes only its temporary deployment. It uses the image configured in the current environment: retain the corresponding image digest with each backup. The archive records configured image names and the running app image ID/registry digests. It never restores over production. Before go-live, practise switching to a separately restored deployment and verify representative users, tickets and attachments. Keep the private deployment environment and certificate provisioning recoverable separately; they are deliberately excluded from the data archive.

docs.title: Update an installation
docs.text:
Stage the chosen release with a restored copy of production data first. Pulling an image does not perform migrations or modify the running installation.

# Set NAFINITY_IMAGE in .env.production to the tested new release or digest.
bin/production pull
bin/production stop app
bin/production-backup /srv/nafinity-backups/before-update
bin/production run --rm --no-deps -T app php vendor/bin/naf db:migrate up
bin/production run --rm --no-deps -T app php vendor/bin/naf rbac:sync
bin/production up -d --wait app
bin/production exec -T app php vendor/bin/naf nafinity:assets:check

Use a new backup directory on each update. If migrations fail, keep the application stopped and inspect the error. An old image can be incompatible with a new schema; rollback means restoring the matching database and storage snapshot as well as the previous image. Do not attach several independently running application deployments to the same storage/database during recovery.

docs.title: If the result is different
docs.text:
Symptom Check Pull returns unauthorized The first GHCR package may still be private; check package visibility and the selected tag. make publish refuses the tags Run make image with the same IMAGE and IMAGE_TAG; both local tags must identify the same image. nginx does not start Check certificate filenames, uid 1000 read permissions and bin/production logs app. App remains unhealthy Run migrations, inspect worker/scheduler logs and verify database/storage access. Login works but account mail fails Check SMTP credentials, sender-domain setup and the provider's delivery logs. Restore verification fails Check backup hashes, retain the backup, and verify with its recorded application image before attempting recovery.

This template covers one application instance. Replicated deployments need separate design and acceptance for sessions, shared storage, queue/scheduler ownership and real client IP handling behind a trusted proxy.

docs.title: Nafinity hours and invoice drafts
docs.text: With naf/board 0.1.6 or newer, export settled personal hours, download invoice positions or prepare a draft in a supported invoicing account. Direct draft creation requires your provider credentials and a separate encryption key in the host configuration.

docs.title: Exporting personal hours
docs.text:
Open your account modal and choose Data export. Select a board or all boards you can currently read, an optional UTC booking-date range and PDF, CSV, text or JSON. The download contains only your booked minutes. Running and paused clocks are not included until settled.

The per-person time journal begins when the new migration is applied. Existing ticket totals and manual edits have no reliable author and booking date and are not included. Bookings keep the original ticket key/title after a transfer or ticket deletion; deleting a project removes its time journal. Read access to the original project is still required.

Export formats use the existing registry. CSV, JSON and text support both tickets and hours; PDF currently supports hours. Plugin formats opt into datasets using ExporterDefinition::sources. All sources share ExportRenderer and the export events; listeners distinguish the source.

The hours file is a neutral time report. Creating an invoice additionally needs customer, seller, prices, taxes and invoice details. EN 16931 is the shared invoice model; XRechnung and ZUGFeRD/Factur-X are relevant invoice formats. Importing time-based invoice lines into an accounting application still needs its own verified adapter or API integration.

docs.title: Exporting invoice items
docs.text:
Open your account modal and choose Export invoice items. Select one board you can currently read, an optional inclusive UTC booking-date range and the format. Enter the EUR net hourly rate and tax percentage explicitly; decimal commas and points are accepted with at most two decimals. Zero is accepted when entered explicitly. For sevdesk, also enter the hourly Unity id from your own account.

The export includes only your settled minutes and groups them by original ticket id, key and title snapshot. Changed titles remain separate. Minutes are summed before conversion to decimal hours. Running timers, manual totals and bookings belonging to other accounts are excluded. The booking dates describe when time was settled and are not a confirmed service period for the invoice.

Format Contents and receiving workflow Neutral CSV Semicolon-separated UTF-8 with BOM, stable headers, exact minutes, hours, HUR, EUR net rate and tax percentage; use a mapped importer or manual preparation Lexware Office JSON Merge lineItems into an invoice draft request; add customer/address, invoice date, currency, tax conditions and service/shipping data sevdesk JSON Merge invoicePosSave into Invoice/Factory/saveInvoice; add the invoice, contact, currency, net pricing and appropriate tax rule easybill JSON Merge items into a document request; net unit prices use cents; add the customer and remaining document details FastBill JSON Merge ITEMS into invoice.create; unit prices use EUR; add CUSTOMER_ID, currency and the correct net/tax settings

The JSON downloads contain API position fragments. They are not complete invoice requests and cannot be uploaded through the tools' web CSV import screens. The receiving integration must authenticate, supply invoice details and handle duplicate submissions. File downloads store no provider credentials and make no provider API calls. For direct draft creation, see direct invoice drafts. Downloading does not mark hours as billed; overlapping exports repeat bookings.

The destination computes the invoice totals. Review rounding before finalizing: neutral hours have six decimal places and Lexware quantities have four, while exact minutes remain in the description. Lexware exports with more than 300 positions are refused; narrow the booking-date range when this happens. FastBill's documented item fields have no unit field; the description includes minutes and hours, and the receiving application configures the unit display. A percentage alone does not establish a tax case; the receiving invoice needs the appropriate invoice-level treatment.

docs.title: Choosing an import route
docs.text:
The providers' documented CSV imports primarily populate contacts or article/service catalogues. They do not carry worked quantities into a particular invoice. The core adapters therefore follow the documented invoice-position APIs:

  • Lexware Office imports and Invoices API.
  • sevdesk imports and API.
  • easybill service imports and REST specification.
  • FastBill product imports, invoice API and item fields.

docs.title: Handing invoices to DATEV
docs.text: The DATEV format handles accounting data; Rechnungsdatenservice 1.0 transfers structured voucher data and/or documents. Neither accepts raw hours as invoice draft positions. Create and review the invoice in the billing tool, then use its supported DATEV handover. A direct DATEV adapter would need a complete invoice or accounting dataset, including the accounting context required by the chosen interface.

docs.title: Extending the export
docs.text: Register an ExporterDefinition with sources: ['invoice-items'] to add a format to the invoice card. The source reuses TimeExportService::bookings() and the existing ExportRenderer, exporter registry and ExportStarted, ExportLine, ExportFinished events. Writers map normalized position data and have no database or network work. Original booking ids remain available to export listeners.

docs.title: Create a draft directly in your invoicing tool
docs.text:
Choose Open invoice drafts in the account modal or the installation's invoice settings. Add an account for Lexware Office, sevdesk, easybill or FastBill. Enter a company name and a company identifier to distinguish accounts. These are local labels; the credentials select the actual issuer, whose address and tax details remain managed in the provider account. A customer ID identifies the recipient, a separate company. Multiple accounts per provider are supported. FastBill also requires the API account email.

Accounts have two billing scopes:

  • Personal: your own settled hours, on a board you can currently read.
  • Company: everyone's settled hours on the selected board. Managing/using shared accounts requires installation settings.manage and exporting another person's hours additionally requires the board's export permission. Installation rights alone do not bypass project access. Separate personal and company claims allow a contractor's submission and the employer's subsequent customer invoice for the same work.

Select the account, one board, optional inclusive UTC booking dates, the existing recipient's provider ID, invoice title and date, explicit service dates, EUR net hourly rate and VAT treatment. The API workflow currently supports standard German VAT at 7/19% and the small-business treatment at 0%; other tax cases remain outside this workflow. sevdesk uses system 2.0 and additionally requires the account's Unity, SevUser and invoice address StaticCountry IDs. Its service period must not end after the invoice date.

The preview reads the existing customer from the provider and shows its returned name, issuer labels, recipient ID, service dates and positions. Bookings already reserved or handed over in the selected billing scope are omitted. Confirming the immutable preview creates one draft. Editing a browser request cannot change the prepared positions or recipient. The preview expires after one hour. API exports allow at most 300 positions and 5000 unclaimed bookings; narrow the dates for larger selections. Exact minutes and people remain in each position description; the provider computes totals and rounding.

Provider Draft operation Authentication Lexware Office POST https://api.lexware.io/v1/invoices?finalize=false Bearer API key sevdesk POST https://my.sevdesk.de/api/v1/Invoice/Factory/saveInvoice, status 100, taxRule 1/11 API key in Authorization easybill POST https://api.easybill.de/rest/v1/documents, type INVOICE Bearer API key FastBill POST https://my.fastbill.com/api/1.0/api.php, service invoice.create Basic auth with email and API key

No adapter finalizes, locks, sends or marks a document paid. easybill's is_draft is read-only; creating the document makes a draft, and Board never calls /done. Review and complete the resulting draft in your provider account before finalizing it there. The provider account needs an API-enabled subscription and appropriate read/create rights.

docs.title: Configure encrypted account storage
docs.text:
The host must provide nafinity:exports:key, a base64-encoded random 32-byte key stored outside the database, and PHP sodium/cURL must be available. In the skeleton this belongs in app/src/config.php (a generic NAF host normally uses app/config.php):

'nafinity' => [
    // Preserve the installation's other nafinity settings.
    'exports' => ['key' => 'ENV:NAFINITY_EXPORT_KEY'],
],

Generate the environment value with php -r 'echo base64_encode(random_bytes(32)), PHP_EOL;'. Keep it with the installation's secrets and backups. XChaCha20-Poly1305 uses NAF's existing OAuth-client Cipher and binds each credential to its account row, owner and provider. Missing/changed keys refuse account storage or decryption; there is no plaintext fallback. Never place keys in a settings field that can be read by browsers. Listing accounts and rendering the page return only labels and scope, never the API key. Disconnect erases the stored credential; separately revoke the key at the provider. An already started handover may still finish. Reconnect after losing or deliberately rotating the encryption key.

docs.title: Duplicate prevention and uncertain results
docs.text:
Before the external write, Board commits unique booking claims and a sending state. Within a billing scope a booking can be claimed once across all providers and accounts. Concurrent confirmations of overlapping previews therefore cannot create two documents. A repeated confirmation of a completed draft returns its receipt. The network request uses native naf/client with retries disabled, verified HTTPS and no redirects; provider URLs are fixed. A disconnected account or lost board/installation rights refuses a new send.

An interruption, rejected request or malformed response retains the claims and shows Check in invoicing tool. A saved sending state also survives a process crash. Board cannot know whether the remote server accepted a timed-out write, so it does not retry automatically. Find the reference Nafinity <preview-id> in the correct provider account. After at least 60 seconds, explicitly record either the existing draft ID or that no draft exists. Only the latter releases the claims; prepare a new preview afterwards. Check carefully before releasing: providers do not offer a shared transactional idempotency contract. A rejection may originate at a proxy after the provider accepted the write.

Recent handovers remain available with their status and external ID. Personal history is private; authorized installation operators share company history, still subject to current board export rights. File downloads remain independent: they neither reserve bookings nor establish that a downloaded file was actually billed. Do not mix manual file imports and API handovers without checking your external account.

docs.title: Extend invoice formats and adapters
docs.text: The versioned invoice extension reference describes ExporterDefinition::sources, draftAdapter and the shared export events. Provider adapters map existing normalized positions; central services retain account authorization, encrypted storage, immutable previews and booking claims.

docs.title: If the result is different
docs.text: Symptom Check Old ticket totals are absent from an hours report The journal begins at migration and contains settled bookings, not historical or manually entered totals. An invoicing account cannot be saved or opened Check PHP sodium/cURL and the unchanged host export encryption key. A draft says Check in invoicing tool Reconcile the external result before releasing claims or preparing another preview; do not blindly repeat the write. A selection exceeds the position limit Narrow the board and booking-date range.

docs.title: Mail replies to Nafinity tickets
docs.text:
This workflow requires naf/board 0.1.6 or newer and naf/mail 0.2.3 or newer. Configure an existing SMTP/IMAP account in your installation; no extra Board integration package is needed.

Nafinity natively polls an existing IMAP mailbox and appends authorized replies as comments to existing tickets. An incoming message never creates a ticket. The installation sends outgoing mail through its configured SMTP provider; Postfix can supply that relay but is not required in the application image. Receiving through an existing mailbox needs no incoming port, public MX record or additional mail server on the Nafinity host.

docs.title: Set up the mailbox
docs.text:
Update the board in the application and migrate its tables:

bin/composer update naf/board naf/mail --with-dependencies
bin/naf db:migrate up

The functionality is part of naf/board; no additional package is required. In source mode the normal Board checkout supplies it through the existing development manifest.

Use a dedicated Nafinity integration account. Its email address does not need a mailbox:

openssl rand -hex 32 | bin/naf nafinity:user mailbot@operator.example 'Mail import'

Add that account to each participating project with permission to read tickets and add comments. Import checks its current permissions each time. The comment author is this account; the comment text identifies the original sender as E-Mail von ….

Configure the skeleton's private .env:

NAFINITY_MAIL_FROM=support@operator.example
NAFINITY_SMTP_HOST=smtp.provider.example
NAFINITY_MAIL_PASSWORD=replace-with-provider-credential

NAFINITY_IMAP_ENABLED=true
NAFINITY_IMAP_HOST=imap.provider.example
NAFINITY_MAIL_ACTOR=mailbot@operator.example

One mail section in app/src/config.php configures outgoing mail and the incoming mailbox. SMTP and IMAP inherit NAFINITY_MAIL_PASSWORD and use NAFINITY_MAIL_FROM as their login. Set NAFINITY_MAIL_USER when the login differs from the sender address. NAFINITY_MAIL_REPLY_TO defaults to the sender and should receive replies in the polled mailbox. Optional NAFINITY_SMTP_USER / NAFINITY_SMTP_PASSWORD and NAFINITY_IMAP_USER / NAFINITY_IMAP_PASSWORD override the shared credentials. Enable ordinary project notifications and emailed invitations with NAFINITY_MAIL_ENABLED=true. Account-security mail and enabled Mail-to-Ticket confirmations use the same sender independently of that notification switch.

Apply the environment and check both connections:

make run
make mail-check
make mail-imap-check

The SMTP check verifies connection, TLS policy and login without sending mail. The IMAP check verifies TLS, login, folder and the existence of the integration account. It neither imports messages nor sends mail. Project membership is configured separately. The existing scheduler queues one poll each minute; each poll examines up to 50 new UIDs.

Password authentication works with providers that enable it, including providers requiring an app password. NAFINITY_IMAP_AUTH=oauth uses the password value as an XOAUTH2 access token. The operator must refresh that token externally and reload the worker environment; the board does not implement a provider-specific OAuth consent or refresh flow. SMTP and IMAP may require different credentials and permissions at the same provider.

docs.title: Create a case and receive a reply
docs.text:
Create a ticket in Nafinity, or open an existing one. Set Anfragende E-Mail-Adresse to the address permitted to reply. That authorized ticket change creates a random public reference, visible as Vorgangsnummer under Information, and queues a generic confirmation to the requester. It contains no internal ticket key, title, description or comment text.

The confirmation subject and body contain:

Vorgangsnummer: V-0123456789ABCDEF01234567

The token shown here is an example, not a case created by an installation. Actual tokens contain 96 bits of randomness and do not encode the internal ticket ID. Ticket-Nr: is accepted as an alternative label only when followed by the same kind of public token; numeric ticket IDs and keys such as ULX-15 are not accepted.

A reply must contain exactly one distinct public reference in its subject or decoded body and exactly one From address matching the ticket's current requester. Repeated occurrences of the same reference are allowed. Domain comparison is case insensitive; local parts, plus tags and aliases remain exact. Changing or clearing the requester revokes the old reference. A replacement requester receives a new one.

An accepted reply adds a plain text comment through Board's existing comment service, including its authorization, activity and notification behavior. The message is marked seen only after the comment and import receipt commit together. Mailbox identity, UIDVALIDITY and UID prevent repeat imports; an identical message with the same Message-ID also stays deduplicated after copying or mailbox recreation. SMTP confirmations can be delivered again if a process stops after delivery but before recording it.

Unknown or ambiguous references, unmatched senders, automatic replies, empty messages and oversized messages stay in the mailbox with their existing flags. Invalid date headers and header conflicts detected as sender spoofing are skipped in the same way. The importer advances past these messages so they cannot block later replies. To revisit them after correcting the ticket configuration, run one bounded rescan and then continue normal polling:

bin/naf nafinity:mail:poll --rescan
bin/naf nafinity:mail:poll

MIME and character sets are decoded. HTML-only mail is converted to text. The whole text, including quoted conversation, is retained; the resulting comment must fit Board's 20,000 character limit. Attachments remain in the mailbox, with a note in the comment. Nothing is deleted or expunged. Internal comments are not automatically forwarded to the requester.

Matching From and a random reference checks the requested routing rule; it is not a cryptographic proof of the sender's identity. Keep the receiving provider's spam and mail authentication controls enabled. The importer does not trust arbitrary Authentication-Results headers as proof.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
IMAP keys live under mail:imap:. The skeleton maps them from environment variables; another host supplies its own configuration with NAF's ENV:NAME references. Shared keys are mail:from, mail:reply_to, mail:username and mail:password. SMTP lives under mail:smtp: and uses Naf\Mail\Core\Transport\SmtpTransport as mail:transport. See Sending mail for the reusable transport's PHP configuration.

Key Skeleton variable Default Effect enabled NAFINITY_IMAP_ENABLED false Enables polling, case generation and confirmation mail. host NAFINITY_IMAP_HOST empty IMAP server hostname. port NAFINITY_IMAP_PORT automatic 993 for SSL, 143 for STARTTLS. security NAFINITY_IMAP_SECURITY ssl ssl or starttls; certificate verification is required. username NAFINITY_IMAP_USER shared login Optional mailbox login override. password NAFINITY_IMAP_PASSWORD shared password Optional password/app password or access-token override. authentication NAFINITY_IMAP_AUTH password Password login or oauth for XOAUTH2. folder NAFINITY_IMAP_FOLDER INBOX One folder to poll. ca_file NAFINITY_IMAP_CA_FILE system trust Optional readable CA bundle inside the container, for a private CA. actor NAFINITY_MAIL_ACTOR empty Active Nafinity integration account email. batch_size host config 50 UIDs examined per poll; 1–200. max_bytes host config 1048576 Maximum complete message size; 1 KiB–10 MiB.

docs.title: Sending with the operator's domain
docs.text:
Use the provider's approved sender as NAFINITY_MAIL_FROM; SMTP defaults to STARTTLS/587 for an external host and implicit TLS when port 465 is selected. naf/mail sends directly from PHP; the image needs no sendmail/msmtp configuration. Its message factory applies the shared sender and Reply-To to all Board mail. Symfony Mailer handles SMTP, MIME and TLS inside naf/mail. Postfix remains an optional relay configured as the SMTP host, normally with explicit NAFINITY_SMTP_AUTH=off for a trusted local relay. This does not create DNS records or guarantee that every provider preserves alignment.

Publish the provider's SPF authorization in the domain's existing single SPF record, enable the provider's DKIM signing and check DMARC alignment using a delivered test message. The provider supplies the required values. SMTP credentials cannot authorize DNS changes; automatic DNS setup requires a DNS-provider integration and explicit access. See the skeleton's docker/mail/smtp.env.example for the configuration example.

docs.title: Mail views
docs.text:
Board renders every email with native view('mail/...') and sends both HTML and a plain-text alternative. Its shared layout supplies the application name, heading, optional reference or verification code, action button and a visible fallback URL. There are views for invitations, notifications, email verification, account-security notices and case confirmations. Dynamic values are escaped inside the layout, including in queue workers.

Override app/src/views/mail/layout.phtml to change the common design, or override an individual view with the same name. PHP and template changes need no image rebuild. Environment changes need make run. The global mail settings show the effective notification switch, sender and registered transport configuration. Administrators can override server values or select Serverkonfiguration to inherit them again. These settings apply to the installation; changes affect new requests, and running workers need restarting.

docs.title: If the result is different
docs.text: Symptom Check The IMAP command is unknown Update naf/board to a release containing the native mail commands. TLS/login fails Check provider IMAP support, hostname, app password/OAuth permissions and trusted CA. No confirmation Enable IMAP, configure SMTP, set the requester through a ticket change, and check the queue. Reply stays in the mailbox Check the public reference, exact From address, automatic-mail headers and message size. Worker reports permission failure Add the active integration account to the ticket's current project with comment permission. Old skipped mail is not retried Use --rescan once, then normal polling to continue through the folder. SMTP connects but delivery fails Confirm the provider permits the sender, then inspect delivered mail authentication and DNS.

docs.title: Working with Nafinity tickets
docs.text: Use naf/board 0.1.7 or newer for Advanced DQL, compact board filters, workspace search, personal views, relevant notifications and the shared ticket editor. Board permissions and version checks apply to every ticket change.

docs.title: Searching across boards
docs.text:
Use the single global search in the top bar to find boards by name or ticket key, and tickets by title, plain description or reference. Enter at least two characters. Suggestions appear after a short pause and are grouped under their board names. Each response replaces the groups dynamically; new boards do not need a predefined result slot. Only boards you can currently read appear. Matching closed tickets and archived tickets or boards remain available.

Use the arrow keys to select a board or ticket and Enter to open it. Escape closes the suggestions. Clearing, closing or changing the search discards earlier answers. Enter without a selected suggestion, the search icon, or Open search results opens a separate result page. That page also works without JavaScript.

Suggestions include at most eight tickets and six additional matching boards. The result page includes at most 50 tickets and 20 matching boards. If more results exist, refine the query. Percent signs and underscores are searched literally.

New ticket appears in the project heading and opens that board's ticket dialog. It uses the same primary action style as New project in the project overview. The action is available only in a writable project; workspace pages and read-only boards omit it. The top bar contains search without a project-name prefix on every application page. The project heading and sidebar identify the current board. The board's Filter control opens dedicated dropdowns. Simple mode has no second text search; Advanced DQL can express the existing board text search. Existing board text-filter links remain valid. Switching modes retains every condition, and Reset clears them with the other filters.

docs.title: Filter a board with dropdowns or DQL
docs.text:
Open Filter above the board to use the dropdowns. Advanced replaces the dropdowns with a DQL field and translates their current values. Press Enter or Apply to run the query. Simple filters validates and applies the query, then fills the dropdowns that can represent its conditions.

status = open AND assignee = me
priority IN (high, urgent) AND due < 2030-01-01
board = NAF AND column = "In Arbeit"
(label = "Design" OR label = "Produkt") AND assignee != none
Property Accepted values status open, closed, archived board Board ticket key, such as NAF, or project id assignee me, none, user id, exact active project member name or email column, swimlane Id or exact displayed name label Id, exact displayed name, or none priority Registered priority id, including contributed priorities title Title equality; ~ matches a literal substring text Existing database fulltext search over title and description, using ~ or = number Positive ticket number; also <, <=, >, >= due, created, updated YYYY-MM-DD; also <, <=, >, >=; due = none finds missing dates

Use =, !=, IN (...) or NOT IN (...) for every property. NOT binds before AND, then OR; parentheses set an explicit order. Property names and keywords are case-insensitive. Value ids and displayed names keep their exact spelling. Quote names containing spaces with single or double quotes. Escape a quote of the same kind or a backslash with a backslash. ticket.status, board.identifier and assigned are aliases for status, board and assignee; q aliases text.

The expression always filters the current authorized board. A board condition cannot turn it into a cross-board search or grant access to another project. Archived tickets remain excluded unless the expression explicitly references the archived status. An open/closed dropdown continues to exclude archives when combined with such an expression. Created/updated comparisons use stored UTC dates.

me means the current reader, including after returning to dropdowns and when another member opens the link. Selecting a named person retains a fixed user id. Conditions involving OR, negation, lists, repeated properties or values a dropdown cannot represent remain visible as additional DQL. Switching modes preserves every condition. Structured plugin filters remain in their original filter envelope, with a visible summary in Advanced.

Queries use one line and reject control characters. They allow up to 2000 characters, 256 tokens, 12 nested groups/negations and 20 values per list. Invalid syntax, properties or values show an editable field error and return HTTP 422. They do not display unfiltered cards. Board cards, counts and live updates use the same query and retain the 300-card display limit.

The Filter disclosure, dropdowns, mode controls and query field remain keyboard operable. Advanced has a field label, a short input hint, expandable help and an announced error message. Native GET forms also support mode switching and filtering without JavaScript.

docs.title: Save and share board views
docs.text:
Open Views beside Filter to manage personal views in the shared dialog. Name the current filter combination and save it. Each person can keep up to 20 views per board. The displayed link contains dropdown filters, DQL and contributed filters, so another project member can open the same view without receiving your bookmark or additional permissions. The recipient's current access is checked when opening it. An assignee = me view means the recipient's assignments when shared.

Views retain core and contributed filters. A removed DQL property returns HTTP 422 instead of widening the saved view. Removing a plugin leaves its saved filter intact; opening that view reports an unknown filter rather than showing a wider result. A stale save asks you to reload instead of overwriting another change. Remove deletes only your bookmark.

docs.title: Find your assignments
docs.text: Choose My tickets in the workspace menu. The list contains your current assignments across all readable, active projects. It starts with open tickets; choose closed or all non-archived tickets and sort by due date or last change. Pages contain up to 50 tickets, including results beyond the board's 300-card display limit. Archived tickets/projects and projects you can no longer read are excluded.

docs.title: Follow tickets
docs.text:
Use naf/board 0.1.8 or newer for the compact eye and followed-ticket overview. The eye beside a ticket's number and status toggles your personal subscription. An accent-colored eye with an outlined background means you follow the ticket; a muted eye means you do not. Its tooltip names the action, and screen readers receive the action label and pressed state. Read-only project members can follow too. Following does not change the ticket version; transferring a ticket clears its subscriptions from the original project.

With JavaScript, toggling the eye preserves the open drawer, keyboard focus and unsaved ticket edits. Native forms remain available without JavaScript.

Choose Followed tickets beside My tickets in the workspace menu to see only tickets you follow. The list spans currently readable, active projects, starts with open tickets and supports closed/all status, due-date/last-change sorting and pages of 50 tickets. Archived tickets/projects and projects you can no longer read are excluded. Assignments and subscriptions remain separate lists.

docs.title: Choose relevant notifications
docs.text:
In personal settings, Notify me about defaults to all project changes. Choose My tickets, mentions and followed tickets to receive changes for tickets you created, are assigned to, follow or are newly mentioned in. Use the ticket eye to follow a ticket. Your personal scope and channel settings still determine whether following produces notifications.

Comment mentions use the displayed member handles. Email addresses do not count, and editing an existing mention does not notify the same person again. Your own changes, inactive memberships, muted projects and disabled channels remain silent. The mail worker checks current preferences and involvement again before delivery. Pre-feature in-app notifications have no relevance classification and remain available in all-changes mode.

docs.title: Use the keyboard and readable card metadata
docs.text:
The first keyboard link skips to the main content. Short choice lists support arrows, Home/End, Enter/Space and Escape; Escape returns focus to their trigger. Use the card action menu to move tickets without dragging, including in filtered or truncated boards.

Card metadata exposes priority, status, due-date purpose and full assignee names to screen readers. Decorative initials and icons stay out of the accessibility tree. Card action targets remain at least 32 × 32 CSS pixels across built-in densities, and built-in label colors retain readable text contrast. Custom themes and CSS need their own accessibility review.

docs.title: Choose the attributes in your ticket view
docs.text:
Open a ticket and choose Deine Ticketansicht anpassen at the bottom of its sidebar. The board settings open Deine Ticketansicht, where you can switch individual attributes on or off and save your choices. The selection belongs to your account in that board; another board and another person's view keep their own selection. Read-only board members can also customize their view.

Attributes retain their existing groups and order. Empty groups disappear. Standard wiederherstellen removes your selection and shows all readable attributes again. Newly registered attributes appear automatically unless you have already stored a choice for that key. Existing read permissions continue to determine which attributes you can choose and see.

Hiding a field changes its display only. Ticket values, exports, other people's views and creation inputs retain their existing behavior. Title, description and comments are fixed ticket areas and stay visible. Hiding tracked time also hides its timer controls; an already running timer continues running. Restore the field to use those controls again.

docs.title: Edit and discuss a ticket
docs.text:
Click the description text to open its editor, as with the title. Links and other interactive content inside the description retain their own actions. The edit control remains available to keyboard users. Board permissions still determine whether editing is available.

The comment composer follows the discussion without covering its last comment. Reply context, comment actions, expanded edit forms and the wrapping composer footer have separate spacing. The composer stays outside the refreshed comment list, preserving an unsent draft when new comments arrive. Sidebar labels and values share their first text baseline, including open inline editors.

docs.title: Create with the same ticket view
docs.text:
+ Neues Ticket opens the shared ticket view with a local draft. The title opens for typing immediately. Description and metadata show their values or muted placeholders. Click Beschreibung einfügen to open one description editor; click an attribute to open its input. Leaving a field updates the draft's display. Escape restores only the field currently being edited to its value when opened. The ticket is saved once you choose Ticket erstellen.

Opening the creation drawer keeps the board address, including its filters. Back closes the drawer through the existing changed-draft confirmation. Reloading returns to the board; changed drafts trigger the browser's native warning before reloading or leaving the page. An untouched draft, an opened empty description editor, and a draft with every change restored do not warn. Once creation succeeds, the address changes to the saved ticket. Open the direct creation address in a new tab for a standalone page; it also remains the fallback without JavaScript.

The drawer and the standalone creation address use ticket.phtml and ticket/field.phtml, as do saved tickets. The shared field component provides the read display and editor container, and the same browser open/close and keyboard handlers serve both modes. Draft fields belong to one native creation form; saved fields retain their existing automatic save forms. Required draft fields open when native validation needs them. Without JavaScript, the native inputs and plain-text description remain available.

The core.extensions asset loads the ticket module once, so it owns one editor registry and one write queue. Quill initializes when the description is first opened and is reused on later edits.

docs.title: Link related tickets
docs.text:
Open a ticket and choose Link ticket. Select a relationship from this ticket's perspective, then open the ticket search. Type a number such as 42, a full key such as NAF-42, or words from its title. Suggestions show the key and title; exact numbers come first. Arrow keys move through the results, Enter selects, and Escape closes the search. Click Link to save.

Relationships include relates to, blocks / is blocked by, duplicates / is duplicated by, clones / is cloned by and resolves / is resolved by. The other ticket shows the corresponding inverse.
